rules.title: Newark rent control ordinance (unverified)
rules.requirement: New Jersey has no statewide rent control, but municipalities may adopt it. Newark is believed to have a local rent control ordinance, but its terms could not be read here, so check the Newark code or the rent control board.
rules.citation: Newark Municipal Code (rent control ordinance; section not stated in documents)
rules.quoted_span: Municipalities may pass an ordinance establishing rent control or rent leveling. Locally created boards enforce these ordinances.
rules.conflict_note: Unverified: Newark's ordinance text was link-only (ecode360 D070-D072). Supporting general proposition quoted from D067; which link holds the rent control chapter is unknown.
rules.review_note: Section, cap formula and dates unknown; do not rely on this without reading the Newark code.

no_rule_findings.finding: No Newark ordinance on algorithmic rent-setting appears in the documents. The state FAIR Act (P.L.2026, c.43, effective 2027-07-01) bars municipalities from enacting conflicting ordinances.
no_rule_findings.quoted_span: A municipality shall be prohibited from enacting an ordinance that conflicts with this act.

parsed.notes: Only state-level documents and three unreadable ecode360 links were provided for Newark. The only city rule added is an unverified, low-confidence rent control record. For the other categories the documents show only state law (NJ deposit, fee, screening and Anti-Eviction Act rules), which applies in Newark and is reported at the state level. Newark's own local ordinances, such as any just-cause or tenant-protection provisions, could not be confirmed.
